newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mixed on uncertainties.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mixed on uncertainties.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed on Wednesday on uncertain short-term market direction ahead of the four-day long Labour Day holiday, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at an intraday high of 3,385 yuan ($408) per tonne, rising 40 yuan. It opened at a low of 3,340 yuan.
May fell 100 yuan to 3,315, July flat at 3,348, November four to 3,394, the January 1998 contract rose six to 3,406, March four to 3,394.
Combined volume rose to 17,700 tonnes from 17,300 tonnes.
Most soybean contracts opened mixed and moved in a narrow range for most of the session, traders said.
"Many investors stayed on the sidelines for the last trading day ahead of the holiday," one trader said. "Retail investors dominated today's trading due to a lack of market-moving news."
Traders said they expected soybeans to continue moving in a narrow range after holiday.
